==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂er-}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*Hreh₁dʰ-}}
{{ety|en|id=book|:inh|enm:reden|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|reden}}, from {{inh|en|ang|rǣdan||to counsel, advise, consult; interpret, read}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*rādan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*rēdaną||advise, counsel}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*Hreh₁dʰ-||to arrange}}.

Cognate with {{cog|sco|rede}}, {{m|sco|red||to advise, counsel, decipher, read}}, {{cog|stq|räide||to advise, counsel}}, {{cog|fy|riede||to advise, counsel}}, {{cog|nl|raden||to advise; guess}}, {{cog|de|raten||to advise; guess}}, {{cog|da|råde||to advise}}, {{cog|sv|råda||to advise, counsel}}, {{cog|fa|رده|tr=rade||to order, to arrange, class}}. In West Germanic the verb had a sense “interpret”, which developed further into “interpret letters” in English and “interpret by intuition, guess” on the continent. Compare {{m|en|rede}}.

====Pronunciation====
* {{enPR|rēd|a=UK,AU,NZ}}, {{IPA|en|/ɹiːd/}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɹid/|a=GA,CA}}
* {{IPA|en|/rɛːd/|/riːd/|a=Early Modern}}<ref>{{R:en:Dobson:1957|II|116|632|passage=(''b'') The variation is commonest in ''read''. It has ''ẹ̄'' in Hart, Laneham, Robinson, Jonson, Price, Cooper, the ‘homophone’ lists of Hodges (‘near alike’; contrast ''EP''), Price, Coles, Strong, Young, Cooper, ''WSC-RS'', Cocker, and Brown. It has ''ę̄'' in the ''ABC for chyldren'', Smith, Bullokar, Gil, Hodges ''EP'' (contrast his ‘near alike’ list in ''SH-PD''), Wallis, Wilkins, the ''Treatise of Stops'' (possibly with a variant ''ẹ̄'')), ''The Protestant Tutor'', and Willis’s rhymelist (see Vol. I, p. 426).|nodot=yes}}</ref>
* {{audio|en|En-uk-to read.ogg|a=UK|text=to read}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-read.ogg|a=US}}
* {{homophones|en|reed|rede}}
* {{rhymes|en|iːd|s=1}}

====Verb====
[[File:Franz Eybl, Lesendes Mädchen.jpg|thumb|upright|A painting of a girl reading.]]
{{en-verb|~s|~ing|[[:en:#Etymology 2|read]]|+,~en<l:archaic,dialectal>}}

# {{lb|en|transitive|or|intransitive}} To [[look at]] and [[interpret]] letters or other information that is [[written]].
#: {{syn|en|interpret|make out|make sense of|understand|scan}}
#: {{ux|en|Have you '''read''' this book?}}
#: {{ux|en|He doesn’t like to '''read'''.}}
## {{lb|en|ergative|of text}} To be [[understood]] or physically read in a specific way.
##: {{ux|en|Arabic '''reads''' right to left.}}
##: {{ux|en|That sentence '''reads''' strangely.}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:National Geographic|year=1989|month=May|volume=175|number=5|title=Braving the Northwest Passage|author=Jeff MacInnis|page=586
|text=Place-names throughout the 4,000-mile-long passage '''read''' like a roster of those who challenged its icy labyrinths of more than 18,000 islands—Baffin, Hudson, Davis, Foxe, Parry, Bylot, Sverdrup.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive|metonymy}} To read a [[work]] or works written by the named [[author]].
##: {{ux|en|At the moment I'm '''reading''' Milton.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1661|author={{w|John Fell (bishop)|John Fell}}|title=The Life of the most learned, reverend and pious Dr. H. Hammond|url=http://archive.org/stream/a615775104worduoft/a615775104worduoft_djvu.txt
|passage=During the whole time of his abode in the university he generally spent thirteen hours of the day in study; by which assiduity besides an exact dispatch of the whole course of philosophy, he '''read''' over in a manner all classic authors that are extant{{...}}}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1982|author=Robert M. Evenson|title="Liberated" Woman"|work=The Cincinnati Enquirer|passage=She '''reads''' ''Playgirl'' magazine, goes to a male-strip joint and then complains about sexual harassment on the job.}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1983
|author=[[w:James Shen|James C. H. Shen]]
|chapter=A Round of Calls
|editor=Robert Myers
|title=The U.S. & Free China: How the U.S. Sold Out Its Ally
|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QGaGAAAAIAAJ
|location=[[Washington, D.C.]]
|publisher=Acropolis Books Ltd.
|ISBN=0-87491-463-9
|page=112
|text=On this occasion he was carrying in his right hand a copy of the English-language ''China News'', an odd touch because the President did not '''read''' English.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|or|intransitive}} To speak [[aloud]] words or other information that is written. {{q|often construed with a ''to'' phrase or an indirect object}}
#: {{syn|en|read [[aloud]]|[[read out]]|read [[out loud]]|[[speak]]}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''read''' us a passage from his new book.}}
#: {{ux|en|All right, class, who wants to '''read''' next?}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=1|passage=In the old days, to my commonplace and unobserving mind, he gave no evidences of genius whatsoever. He never '''read''' me any of his manuscripts, {{...}} and therefore my lack of detection of his promise may in some degree be pardoned.}}
#* {{RQ:Travers Cuckoo in the Nest|chapter=1|passage=He '''read''' the letter aloud. Sophia listened with the studied air of one for whom, even in these days, a title possessed some surreptitious allurement. {{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[interpret]], or [[infer]] a [[meaning]], [[significance]], [[thought]], [[intention]], etc., from.
#: {{ux|en|She '''read''' my mind and promptly rose to get me a glass of water.}}
#: {{ux|en|I can '''read''' his feelings in his face.}}
# To [[consist]] of certain [[text]].
#: {{syn|en|say|run}}
#: {{ux|en|On the door hung a sign that '''read''' "No admittance".}}
# {{lb|en|ergative}} To [[substitute]] a corrected piece of text in place of an [[erroneous]] one; {{n-g|used to introduce an emendation of a text}}.
#: {{syn|en|sic pro}}
#*: The sign of coefficient ''a''(3) in the general formula of Table 2 should be plus instead of minus. Thus, the formula should '''read'''{{...}}
## {{lb|en|by extension|ironic|or|humorous|usually|imperative}} {{non-gloss|Used to introduce a blunter, actually intended meaning}}.
##: {{ux|en|Our school focuses primarily on the liberal arts ('''read''' "useless degrees").}}
##* {{RQ:Time|title=From Tickle Me Elmo to Squinkies: Top 10 Toy Crazes|author=Tamara Weston|date=December 23 2010
|text=Parents, meanwhile, deplored [Bratz dolls] as far too adult ('''read''': slutty) for kids, accusing the doe-eyed, pouty-lipped toys of fostering unhealthy body images among young girls.
|url=https://content.time.com/time/specials/packages/article/0,28804,1947621_1947626_1947688,00.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260222145709/https://content.time.com/time/specials/packages/article/0,28804,1947621_1947626_1947688,00.html|archivedate=22 February 2026}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|telecommunications}} To be able to [[hear]] what another person is saying over a [[radio]] connection.
#: {{syn|en|copy|hear|receive}}
#: {{ux|en|Do you '''read''' me?}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|rail}} To [[observe]] and [[comprehend]] (a displayed [[signal]]).
#: {{ux|en|A repeater signal may be used where the track geometry makes the main signal difficult to '''read''' from a distance.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|Commonwealth|except Scotland}} To [[study]] (a subject) at a high level, especially at [[university]].
#: {{syn|en|learn|study}}
#: {{ux|en|I am '''reading''' theology at university.}}
# {{lb|en|computing|transitive}} To [[fetch#Verb|fetch]] [[data]] from (a storage medium, ''etc.'').
#: {{ux|en|to '''read''' a hard disk}}
#: {{ux|en|to '''read''' a port}}
#: {{ux|en|to '''read''' the keyboard}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|LGBTQ}} To [[recognise]] (someone) as being [[transgender]].
#: {{syn|en|clock}}
#: {{ux|en|Every time I go outside, I worry that someone will '''read''' me.}}
# {{lb|en|at first especially in the black|_|LGBTQ|_|community}} To call [[attention]] to the [[flaw]]s of (someone) in a [[playful]], [[taunting]], or [[insulting]] way.
#*: Snapping, we are told, comes from '''''reading''''', or exposing hidden flaws in a person's life, and out of '''reading''' comes ''shade'' {{...}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2003|author=Philip Auslander|title=Performance: Media and technology|page=179|passage=CB [a black gay person being quoted]: "So, one time I '''read''' him and we were standing downstairs at the front desk in the dorm and I '''read''' him and there was this little bell {{...}}." In the first example, the interviewee [CB] used snapping to '''read''' his white friend in a playful way, {{...}}.}}
# {{lb|en|go}} To imagine [[sequence]]s of potential [[move]]s and responses without actually placing [[stone]]s.
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[think]], [[believe]]; to [[consider]] (that).
#* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=II|canto=I|text=But now, faire Ladie, comfort to you make, / And '''read'''{{...}} / That short reuenge the man may ouertake {{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[advise]]; to counsel. See {{m|en|rede}}.
#* {{RQ:Tyndale Obedience|chapter=The .IIIJ. Senses of yͤ Scripture|folio=cxlvi|verso=1|passage=[T]herfore / I '''red''' the [thee] / gete the [thee] to Gods vvorde ãd [and] therby trye all doctrine and agenſt that receave nothinge.}}
#* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=I|canto=I|page=6|text=This is the wandring wood, this ''Errours den'', / A monster vile, whom God and man does hate: / Therefore I '''read''' beware.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To tell; to [[declare]]; to [[recite]].
#* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=II|canto=IV|text=But '''read''' how art thou named, and of what kin.}}
# {{lb|en|video games}} To predict another player's actions before they perform them or before they are apparent.

=====Usage notes=====
* Unlike the much less common {{m|en|sic pro}} which is set off in square brackets, admonitions for the reader to emend a quote to ''read'' a separate meaning are typically put within parentheses.
* [[#Etymology_2|The past tense and participle]] are pronounced /ɹɛd/.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# A reading or an act of reading, especially of an actor's part of a play or a piece of stored data.
#: {{ux|en|I had a '''read''' of the evening papers.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1879|author=w:Frederick James Furnivall|journal=letter to the editor of "The Spectator"
|passage=One newswoman here lets magazines for a penny a '''read'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1958|author=w:Philip Larkin|title=Self's the Man
|passage=And when he finishes supper / Planning to have a '''read''' at the evening paper / It's ''Put a screw in this wall''— / He has no time at all{{...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2006|title=MySQL administrator's guide and language reference|page=393
|passage=In other words, the system can do 1200 '''reads''' per second with no writes, the average write is twice as slow as the average read, and the relationship is linear.}}
# {{lb|en|in combination}} Something to be read; a written work.
#: {{ux|en|His thrillers are always a gripping '''read'''.}}
# A person's [[interpretation]] or [[impression]] of something.
#: {{ux|en|What's your '''read''' of the current political situation?}}
#: {{ux|en|On the quarterback's first '''read''' of the situation, his target receiver was not open.}}
# {{lb|en|at first especially in the black|_|LGBTQ|_|community}} An instance of {{l|en|read|reading|calling attention to someone's flaws; a taunt or insult}}.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2013|author=bell hooks|title=Teaching Critical Thinking: Practical Wisdom| isbn=1135263493| passage=I learned that it was acceptable to be witty, especially if you were one of the wearblackallthetime, deconstructivist, radical, feministbitchydiva girls who could give a harsh '''read''' (i.e., critique) or throw shade {{...}}.}}
# {{lb|en|biochemistry}} The [[identification]] of a specific [[sequence]] of [[gene]]s in a [[genome]] or [[base]]s in a [[nucleic acid]] string.
